G3600.def:
ὀδυνάω, -ῶ
(ὀδύνη), [in LXX: Zacharie 9:5 (חוּל), Zacharie 12:10 (מָרַר hi.), La 1:13 (דָּוֶה), Wis.14:24, al. ;] 
to cause pain or suffering; pass. and mid., to suffer pain, be tormented or greatly distressed: Luc 2:48 16:24-25 (ὀδυνᾶσαι, see M, Pr., 53 f.); before ἐπί, Actes 20:38.†

G3601.def:
ὀδύνη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX for יָגוֹן, מַר, etc. (26 words in all) ;] 
pain, distress, of body or mind : Romains 9:2, 1 Timothée 6:10.†

G3602.def:
ὀδυρμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ὀδύρομαι, to lament), [in LXX : Jérémie 31:15 (תַּמְרוּר), 2Ma.11:6 * ;] 
lamentation, mourning: Matthieu 2:18 (LXX), 2 Corinthiens 7:7.†

G3604.def:
Ὀζείας (Rec. Ὀζίας), -ου, ὁ (Heb. עֻזִּיָּה), 
Uzziah: Matthieu 18:1-35 9:1-38.†

G3605.def:
ὄζω 
[in LXX: Exode 8:14 (בָּאַשׁ)* ;] 
to smell (i.e. emit a smell): Jean 11:39.†

G3607.def:
ὀθόνη, -ης, ἡ
(of Semitic origin, cf. Heb. אֵטוּן, yarn) 
__1. fine linen (Hom., al.). 
__2. Later, a sheet or sail: Actes 10:11 11:5.†

G3608.def:
ὀθόνιον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of ὀθόνη, which see), [in LXX: Juges 14:13 (סָדִין), Osée 2:5, 9 (פִּשְׁתֶּה)* ;] 
a piece of fine linen, a linen cloth; Luc 24:12 (WH, R, mg., om.), Jean 19:40 20:5-7.†

G3610.def:
οἰκέτης, -ου, ὁ
(οἰκέω), [in LXX for עֶבֶד ;] 
a house-servant: Luc 16:13, Romains 14:4; pl., Actes 10:7, 1 Pierre 2:18 (In Plat., Hdt., Sir.4:30 6:11, the pl. includes all the inmates of the house, the familia, οἰκετεία.)†
SYN.. see: διάκονος

G3611.def:
οἰκέω, -ῶ
(οἶκος), [in LXX chiefly for יָשַׁב ;] 
__(a) trans., to inhabit: with accusative, 1 Timothée 6:16; 
__(b) intrans., to dwell: before μετά (of married life), 1 Corinthiens 7:12-13; metaphorically, before ἐν: ἀγαθόν, Romains 7:18; ἁμαρτία, Romains 7:20; πνεῦμα θεοῦ, Romains 8:9, 11, 1 Corinthiens 3:16 (cf. ἐν-, κατ-, ἐν-κατ-, παρ-, περι-, συν-οικέω).†

G3612.def:
οἴκημα, -τος, τό
(οἰκέω), [in LXX: Eze.16:24 (גַב), Tob.2:4, Wis.13:15 * ;] 
a dwelling. As a euphemism for other definite terms (e.g. brothel. Hdt., ii, 121; cf. Ez, l.with), a prison (Thus., iv, 47 f.); Actes 12:7.†

G3613.def:
οἰκητήριον, -ου, τό
(οἰκητήρ = οἰκήτωρ, an inhabitant), [in LXX: 2Ma.11:2, 3Ma.2:15 * ;] 
a habitation: Ju 6; trop., 2 Corinthiens 5:2.†

G3614G.def:
οἰκία, -ας, ἡ
(οἶκος), [in LXX chiefly (very freq.) for בַּיִת ;] 
a house, dwelling: Matthieu 2:11 7:24-27, Marc 1:29, al.; ἐν οἰκίᾳ (= cl. κατ ̓ οἰκίαν), at home, Luc 8:27; εἰς οἰ., II Jn 10; οἰ, with genitive of person(s), usually has the art. (Matthieu 8:14, al., but cf. οἶκος and see Bl., § 46, 9); ἡ οἰ. τ. πατρός μου, Jean 14:2. 
Metaphorical, 
__(a) of the body as the dwelling of the soul: 2 Corinthiens 5:1; 
__(b) of property (as בַּיִת, Genèse 45:18, LXX, τ. υπάρχοντα; 3Ki.13:8, LXX, οἶκος) = οἶκος (which see): Marc 12:40, Luc 20:47; 
__(with) of the inmates of the dwelling, the household: Matthieu 12:25; with genitive of person(s), Jean 4:53, 1 Corinthiens 16:15 
SYN.: οἶκος, which in Attic law denoted the whole estate, οἰκία, the dwelling only. In cl. poets οἶκος has also the latter sense, but not in prose, except in metaphorically usage, where it signifies both property and household. The foregoing distinction is not, however, consistently maintained in late Greek; cf. MM, ii, xvii, and see Thayer, see word οἰκία

G3614H.def:
οἰκία, -ας, ἡ
(οἶκος), [in LXX chiefly (very freq.) for בַּיִת ;] 
a house, dwelling: Matthieu 2:11 7:24-27, Marc 1:29, al.; ἐν οἰκίᾳ (= cl. κατ ̓ οἰκίαν), at home, Luc 8:27; εἰς οἰ., II Jn 10; οἰ, with genitive of person(s), usually has the art. (Matthieu 8:14, al., but cf. οἶκος and see Bl., § 46, 9); ἡ οἰ. τ. πατρός μου, Jean 14:2. 
Metaphorical, 
__(a) of the body as the dwelling of the soul: 2 Corinthiens 5:1; 
__(b) of property (as בַּיִת, Genèse 45:18, LXX, τ. υπάρχοντα; 3Ki.13:8, LXX, οἶκος) = οἶκος (which see): Marc 12:40, Luc 20:47; 
__(with) of the inmates of the dwelling, the household: Matthieu 12:25; with genitive of person(s), Jean 4:53, 1 Corinthiens 16:15 
SYN.: οἶκος, which in Attic law denoted the whole estate, οἰκία, the dwelling only. In cl. poets οἶκος has also the latter sense, but not in prose, except in metaphorically usage, where it signifies both property and household. The foregoing distinction is not, however, consistently maintained in late Greek; cf. MM, ii, xvii, and see Thayer, see word οἰκία

G3615.def:
οἰκιακός (in Plut., al., -ειακός), ή, όν 
(οἰκία), = οἰκεῖος 
belonging to the household, one's own: Matthieu 10:36; opposite to οἰκοδεσπότης, Matthieu 10:25.†

G3616.def:
οἰκο-δεσποτέω, -ῶ
(οἰκοδεσπότης) 
to rule a household: 1 Timothée 5:14.†

G3617.def:
οἰκο-δεσπότης, -ου, ὁ
(οἶκος, δεσπότης), 
the master of a house, a householder: Matthieu 10:25 13:27 20:11 24:43, Marc 14:14, Luc 12:39 13:25 14:21; ἄνθρωπος οἰ., Matthieu 13:52 20:1 21:33; pleonast., oἰ. τ. οἰκίας, Luc 22:11 (see Bl., § 81, 4).†

G3618.def:
οἰκοδομέω, -ῶ
(οἰκοδόμος), [in LXX chiefly for בָּנָה ;] 
to build a house, to build: absol., Luc 11:48 14:30 17:28; οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες, the builders (as Psaumes 118:22, בָּנָה), Matthieu 21:42, Marc 12:10, Luc 20:17, 1 Pierre 2:7" (LXX) ; ἐ π ̓ ἀλλότριον θεμέλιον οἰ., proverb., Romains 15:20; with accusative of thing(s), Galates 2:18; πύργον), Matthieu 21:33, Marc 12:1, Luc 14:28; ἀποθήκας, Luc 12:18; ναόν, Marc 14:58; pass., Jean 2:20; οἰκία, Luc 6:48; with accusative of thing(s) before dative of person(s) (cf. Genèse 8:20, Eze.16:24), Luc 7:5, Actes 7:47, 49; accusative before ἐπί, Matthieu 7:24, 26 Luc 6:49; πόλιν ἐπ ̓ ὄρους, Luc 4:29; of rebuilding, or restoring, Matthieu 23:29 26:61 27:40, Marc 15:29, Luc 11:47, Metaphorical, τ. ἐκκλησίαν, Matthieu 16:18; of the growth of Christian character (cf. בָּנָה, in Psaumes 28:5, Jérémie 24:6, al.), to build up (AV, edify): absol., Actes 20:32, 1 Corinthiens 8:1 10:23; with accusative of person(s), 1 Corinthiens 14:4, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:11; pass., Actes 9:31, 1 Corinthiens 14:17, 1 Pierre 2:5; of blameworthy action (AV, embolden), 1 Corinthiens 8:10 (cf. ἀν-, ἐπ-, συν-οικοδομέω).†
οἰκο-δόμος, -ου, ὁ 
(οἶκος + δέμω, to build), [in LXX for בָּנָה, etc. ;] 
a builder: Actes 4:11.†

G3619.def:
οἰκοδομή, -ῆς, ἡ
(οἶκος, + δέμω, to build), [in LXX: 1 Chroniques 29:1 A (בִּירָה), Eze.17:17 40:2 (בָּנָה, מִבְנֶה), Sir.22:16 40:19, al. ;] 
= cl. οἰκοδομία (which see), -δόμησις (Thuc., Plat.), 
__1. the act of building; in NT always metaphorically, building up, edifying: Romains 14:19 15:2, 1 Corinthiens 14:26, 2 Corinthiens 10:8 13:10, Éphésiens 4:29; with genitive obj., 1 Corinthiens 14:12, 2 Corinthiens 12:19, Éphésiens 4:12, 16; λαλεῖν, λαβεῖν, οἰ., 1 Corinthiens 14:3. 
__2. = οἰκοδόμημα, a building: Matthieu 24:1, Marc 13:1-2; metaphorically, 1 Corinthiens 3:9, 2 Corinthiens 5:1, Éphésiens 2:21.†

G3621.def:
οἰκονομέω, -ῶ
(οἰκονόμος), [in LXX: Psaumes 112:5 (כּוּל pilp.), 2Ma.3:14 * ;] 
to manage as house-steward, be a steward: absol., Luc 16:2; hence, generally (see: οἰκονομία), to manage, regulate, arrange (cl., 2Mac, Lc., 3Ma.3:2 R).†

G3622.def:
οἰκονομία, -ας, ἡ
(οἰκονομέω), [in LXX: Ésaïe 22:19, 21 (מַצָּב, מֶמְשָׁלָה)* ;] 
__1. prop. (Plat., Arist.), the office of οἰκονόμος, stewardship: Luc 16:2-4. 
__2. In later writers (Plut., al.; see AR on Éphésiens 1:10; MM, xviii), generally, administration, dispensation: 1 Corinthiens 9:17, Éphésiens 1:10 3:2, 9, Colossiens 1:25, 1 Timothée 1:4.†

G3623.def:
οἰκονόμος, -ου, ὁ
(οἶκος + νέμω, to manage) [in LXX chiefly for עַל ;] 
__1. prop., the manager of a household or estate, a house- or land-steward (usually a slave or freedman): Luc 12:42 16:1, 3 16:8, 1 Corinthiens 4:2, Galates 4:2; ὀ οἰ. τ. πόλεως (RV, treasurer; cf. I Esther 4:49), Romains 16:23. 
__2. Metaphorical (in wider sense; cf. οἰκονομία), an administrator, a steward: of Christian ministers, 1 Corinthiens 4:1, Tite 1:7; of Christians generally, 1 Pierre 4:10.†

G3624G.def:
οἶκος, -οῦ, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for בַּיִת, also for אֹהֶל ,הֵכָל, etc. ;] 
__1. prop., a house, dwelling: Actes 2:2 19:16; with genitive poss., Matthieu 9:6, 7 Marc 2:11, Luc 1:23, al.; with genitive attrib., ἐμπορίου, Jean 2:16; προσευχῆς, Matthieu 21:13, al.; of a sanctuary (Hdt., Eur.): οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, of the tabernacle, Matthieu 12:4, al.; the temple, Matthieu 21:13, al.; metaphorically of a city: Matthieu 23:38, Luc 13:35; of the body, Matthieu 12:44, Luc 11:24; of Christians, 1 Pierre 2:5; ἐν οἴ (M, Pr., 81f.), at home, Marc 2:1, 1 Corinthiens 11:34 14:35; so κατ ̓ οἶκον, Actes 2:46 5:42; οἱ εἰς (= οἱ ἐν; see: εἰς) τ. οἶ., Luc 7:10 15:6; κατ ̓οἴκους, from house to house, Actes 8:3 20:20; εἰς (κατ ̓) οἶκον, with genitive (Bl., §46, 9), Marc 8:3, Luc 14:1, Romains 16:5, al. 
__2. By meton., a house, household, family: Luc 10:5, Actes 7:10, 1 Corinthiens 1:16, 1 Timothée 3:4, 5 al.; of the Church, ὁ οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, 1 Timothée 3:15, Hébreux 3:2, 1 Pierre 4:17; of descendants, οἶ Ἰσραήλ (Δαυείδ, Ἰακώβ; Bl, §47, 9), Matthieu 10:6, Luc 1:27, 33 al. (cf. Exode 6:14, 1 Rois 2:30, al.). 
SYN.: see: οἰκία.

G3624H.def:
οἶκος, -οῦ, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for בַּיִת, also for אֹהֶל ,הֵכָל, etc. ;] 
__1. prop., a house, dwelling: Actes 2:2 19:16; with genitive poss., Matthieu 9:6, 7 Marc 2:11, Luc 1:23, al.; with genitive attrib., ἐμπορίου, Jean 2:16; προσευχῆς, Matthieu 21:13, al.; of a sanctuary (Hdt., Eur.): οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, of the tabernacle, Matthieu 12:4, al.; the temple, Matthieu 21:13, al.; metaphorically of a city: Matthieu 23:38, Luc 13:35; of the body, Matthieu 12:44, Luc 11:24; of Christians, 1 Pierre 2:5; ἐν οἴ (M, Pr., 81f.), at home, Marc 2:1, 1 Corinthiens 11:34 14:35; so κατ ̓ οἶκον, Actes 2:46 5:42; οἱ εἰς (= οἱ ἐν; see: εἰς) τ. οἶ., Luc 7:10 15:6; κατ ̓οἴκους, from house to house, Actes 8:3 20:20; εἰς (κατ ̓) οἶκον, with genitive (Bl., §46, 9), Marc 8:3, Luc 14:1, Romains 16:5, al. 
__2. By meton., a house, household, family: Luc 10:5, Actes 7:10, 1 Corinthiens 1:16, 1 Timothée 3:4, 5 al.; of the Church, ὁ οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, 1 Timothée 3:15, Hébreux 3:2, 1 Pierre 4:17; of descendants, οἶ Ἰσραήλ (Δαυείδ, Ἰακώβ; Bl, §47, 9), Matthieu 10:6, Luc 1:27, 33 al. (cf. Exode 6:14, 1 Rois 2:30, al.). 
SYN.: see: οἰκία.

G3627.def:
οἰκτείρω
(οἶκτος, pity), [in LXX for רָחַם pi., חָנַן, etc. ;] 
to pity, have compassion on. with accusative of person(s), Romains 9:15 (LXX).†
SYN.: ἐλεέω, q.v

G3628.def:
οἰκτιρμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(οἰκτείρω), [in LXX, usually in pl., chiefly for רַחַם ;] 
compassion, pity. σπλάγχνα οἰκτιρμοῦ, a heart of compassion, Colossiens 3:12; in pl. (as LXX for Heb. רַחַם), οἰ. τ. θεοῦ, Romains 12:1, Hébreux 10:28; ό πατὴρ τῶν οἰ, 2 Corinthiens 1:3; σπλάγχνα κ. οἰ., Philippiens 2:1.†
SYN.: ἔλεος, q.v

G3629.def:
οἰκτίρμων, -ον
(οἰκτείρω), in cl. poët, for ἐλεήμων (which see), [in LXX chiefly for רַחוּם ;] 
merciful: Luc 6:36, Jacques 5:1.†

G3630.def:
οἰνο-πότης, -ου, ὁ
(οίνος + πότης, a drinker), poët. and late prose, [in LXX: Proverbes 23:20 (יַיִן סָבָא)* ;] 
a wine-drinker, wine-bibber: Matthieu 11:19, Luc 7:34.†

G3631.def:
οἶνος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for יַיִן also for תִּירוֹשׁ, etc. ;] 
wine; Matthieu 9:17, Luc 1:15, Jean 2:3, al.; οἴνῳ προσέχειν, 1 Timothée 3:8; δουλοῦσθαι, Tite 2:3. Metaphorical, Apocalypse 14:8, 10 16:19 17:2 18:3 19:15. By meton. for ἄμπελος, Apocalypse 6:6

G3632.def:
οἰνοφλυγία, -ας, ἡ
(φλύω, to bubble up, overflow), cf. -γέω, Deutéronome 21:20 
drunkenness, debauchery: 1 Pierre 4:3.†
SYN.: see: κραιπάλη

G3633.def:
οἴομαι, οἶμαι 
[in LXX for הִנֵּה, Genèse 37:7, al. ;] 
to suppose, expect, imagine; with accusative and inf., Jean 21:25; with inf., Philippiens 1:17; before ὅτι, Jacques 1:7.†
οἶμαι, see: οἴομαι 
SYN.. see: ἡγέομαι

G3634.def:
οἷος, -α, -ον 
relat. pron., qualitative (related to ὅς as qualis to qui), what sort or manner of, such as, in NT usually without its correl. τοιοῦτος : Matthieu 24:21, Marc 9:3, 2 Corinthiens 12:20, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:5, 2 Timothée 3:11, Apocalypse 16:18; before τοιοῦτος, 1 Corinthiens 15:48 15:2 2 Corinthiens 10:11; id. redundant, Marc 13:19; τ. αὑτὸν . . . σἷον, Philippiens 1:30; οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι, elliptically, but it is not as though (RV), Romains 9:6.†

G3635.def:
ὀκνέω, -ῶ
(ὄκνος, shrinking, hesitation), [in LXX: Nombres 22:16 (מָנַע ni.), Juges 18:9 (אָצַל ni.), Tob.12:6, 13, Jdth.12:13, Sir.7:35, 4Ma.14:4 * ;] 
to shrink from doing, hesitate to do (Hom., Thuc., al.); hence, to delay with inf., Actes 9:38 (cf. Nu, l.with, and see MM, xviii).†

G3636.def:
ὀκνηρός, -ά, -όν
(ὀκνέω), [in LXX forPro.6:6, 9 al. ;] 
shrinking, hesitating, timid: with dative (Bl., § 38, 2), Romains 12:11; hence, slothful: Matthieu 25:26. Of things, that which causes shrinking, irksome: Philippiens 3:1.†

G3637.def:
ὀκταήμερος, -ον
(ὀκτώ, ἡμέρα), 
of the eighth day, eight days old: with dative ref., περιτομῇ., Philippiens 3:5 (words of this class denote duration, cf. τεταρταῖος).†

G3638.def:
ὀκτώ, οἱ, αἱ, τά
indecl., 
eight: Luc 2:21, Jean 5:5, al

G3639.def:
ὄλεθρος, -ον 
(ὄλλυμι, to destroy), [in LXX for שֹׁד. שָׁדַד, etc. ;] 
ruin, destruction, death: 1 Thessaloniciens 5:3, 1 Timothée 6:9; αἰώνιος, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:9 (L, txt., ὀλέθριος, which see); εἰς ὄ. τῆς σαρκός, for physical discipline, to destroy carnal lusts, 1 Corinthiens 5:5.†

G3640.def:
ὀλιγό-πιστος, -ον 
of little faith or trust: Matthieu 6:30 8:26 14:31 16:8, Luc 12:28.†

G3641.def:
ὀλίγος, -η, -ον
(on οὐχ ὁλ., see infr.), [in LXX chiefly for מָעַט ;] 
of number, quantity, size, few, little, small, slight: Matthieu 9:37 15:34, Marc 6:5 8:7, Luc 10:2 12:48 (sc. πληγάς, opposite to πολλάς), 1 Timothée 5:23, Hébreux 12:10, Apocalypse 3:4 12:12; οὐκ ὀ. (in the best uncials written οὐκ ὁ.; see WH, App., 143; M, Pr., 44; Thackeray, Gr., 126 f.), Actes 12:18 14:28 15:2 (with genitive part.) Actes 17:4, 12 19:23-24 27:20; pl., absol., Matthieu 7:14 20:16 (WH, txt., RV, om.) Matthieu 22:14, Luc 13:23, 1 Pierre 3:20. Neut. sing (τὸ) ὀ.: Luc 7:47, 2 Corinthiens 8:15; πρὸς ὀλίγον, 1 Timothée 4:8, Jacques 4:14; ἐν ὀ., Actes 26:28-29 (with little effort; see Page, in l); id., in brief, Éphésiens 3:3; adverbially, ὀλίγον, of time, Marc 6:31, 1 Pierre 1:6 5:10, Apocalypse 17:10; of space, Marc 1:19, Luc 5:3; pl., ὀλίγα, Luc 10:42, Apocalypse 2:14; ἐπ᾽ ὀλίγα, Matthieu 25:21, 23; δι᾽ ὀλίγων, in few words, briefly, 1 Pierre 5:12 (cf. Plat., Legg., vi, 778 e).†
**ὀλίγως, adv. 
(ὀλίγος), [in Aq.: Ésaïe 10:7 * ;] 
a little, almost, all but: 2 Pierre 2:18.†

G3642.def:
ὀλιγόφυχος, -ον
[in LXX: Ésaïe 35:4 (מָהַר ni.), etc. ;] 
faint-hearted: 1 Thessaloniciens 5:14.†

G3643.def:
ὀλιγωρέω, -ῶ
(ὀλίγος + ὤρα, care), [in LXX: Proverbes 3:11 (מָאַס)* ;] 
to esteem lightly, think little of: with genitive, Hébreux 12:5 (LXX),†

G3644.def:
ὀλοθρευτής (Rec. όλ-), -οῦ, ὁ 
(ὀλοθρεύω), 
a destroyer: 1 Corinthiens 10:10 (not elsewhere).†

G3645.def:
ὀλοθρεύω
(ὄλεθρος), late (Alex.) form of ὄλεθρεύω ω (cf. MGr., ξολοθρεύω) [in LXX for כָּרַת, שָׁחַת hi., etc. ;] 
to destroy: Hébreux 11:28 (cf. ἐξ-ολοθρεύω).†
ὀλεθρεύω, see: ὀλοθρεύω 
ὀλοθρεύω
(ὄλεθρος), late (Alex.) form of ὄλεθρεύω ω (cf. MGr., ξολοθρεύω) [in LXX for כָּרַת, שָׁחַת hi., etc. ;] 
to destroy: Hébreux 11:28 (cf. ἐξ-ολοθρεύω).†
ὀλεθρεύω, see: ὀλοθρεύω

G3646.def:
ὁλοκαύτωμα, -τος, τό
(ὅλος, καίω), [in LXX chiefly for עֹלָה ;] 
a whole burnt offering: Marc 12:33, Hébreux 10:6, 8" (LXX) (of. Kennedy, Sources, 113 f.).†
SYN.: see: θυσία

G3647.def:
ὀλοκληρία, -ας, ἡ
(ὁλόκληρος), [in LXX: Ésaïe 1:6 (מְתֹם)* ;] 
completeness, soundness: Actes 3:16.†

G3648.def:
ὁλό-κληρος, -ον
(ὅλος, κλῆρος, i.e. with all that has fallen by lot), [in LXX: Lévitique 23:15, Eze.15:5 (תָּמִים), Deutéronome 27:6, Josué 8:31 (9:2) (שָׁלֵם), Zacharie 11:16 (נָצַב ni.), Wis.15:3, 1Ma.4:47, 4Ma.15:17 * ;] 
complete, entire; in NT in ethical sense (as Wis, 4Mac, ll. with), 1 Thessaloniciens 5:23; ὁ. καὶ τέλειοι, Jacques 1:4.†
SYN.: ὁλοτελής (which see), τελειος (Tr., Syn., § xxii)

G3649.def:
ὀλολύζω
(onomatop.), [in LXX chiefly for יָלַל hi. ;] (in Hom., of women crying to the gods in prayer or thanksgiving), 
to cry aloud: Jacques 5:1.†

G3651.def:
ὁλοτελής, -ές
(ὅλος, τίλος), 
complete, perfect.. 1 Thessaloniciens 5:23.†
SYN.: ὁλόκληρος (which see), τέλειος. "As regards meaning, ὁλόκληρος can hardly be distinguished from ὁλοτελής though, in accordance with its derivation, it draws more special attention to the several parts to which the wholeness spoken of extends, no part being wanting or lacking in completeness" (M, Th., 78)

G3652.def:
Ὀλυμπᾶς
(perh. contr. fr. Ὀλνμπιόδωρος, Bl., § 29), -ᾶ, 
Olympas: Romains 16:15.†

G3653.def:
ὄλυνθος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Cantique des cantiques 2:13 (פַּג)* ;] 
an unripe fig, which grows in winter and usually falls off in the spring : Apocalypse 6:13.†

G3654.def:
ὅλως 
adv. (ὅλος), 
altogether, assuredly, actually (with neg., at all) : Matthieu 5:34, 1 Corinthiens 5:1 6:7 15:29.†

G3655.def:
ὄμβρος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 32:2 (שָׂעִיר), Wis.16:16, al. ;] 
a storm of rain, a shower: Luc 12:54.†

G3656.def:
ὁμιλέω, -ῶ
(ὅμιλος), [in LXX: Proverbes 5:19 (רָוָה pi.), al. ;] 
to be in company with, consort with; hence, to converse with: Actes 20:11; with dative, Actes 24:26; before πρός, Luc 24:14-15.†

G3657.def:
όμιλία, -ας, ή
(όμιλος), [in LXX: Exode 21:10 (עוֹנָה), al. ;] 
company, association: 1 Corinthiens 15:33.†

G3658.def:
ὅμιλος, -ου, ὁ 
[in Aq. : 1 Rois 19:20 * ;] 
a crowd, throng: Apocalypse 18:17, Rec.†

G3660.def:
ὀμνύω
(so Hdt. and some Att.. writers) and ὄμνυμι (so generally in Att.. prose and always in Trag.; Marc 14:71, -ύναι), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁבַע ni. ;] 
to swear, affirm by oath: Matthieu 26:74, Marc 14:71, Hébreux 7:21; before εἰ (q.v), Hébreux 3:11 4:3; with dative of person(s), Marc 6:23; id. with inf., Hébreux 3:18; before ὅρκῳ, Actes 2:30; ὀ. ὅρκον, πρός, with accusative of person(s) (cl.), Luc 1:73; with accusative (of that by which one swears; cl., see MM, xviii), Jacques 5:12; before κατά, with genitive (LXX; Bl., § 34, 1), Hébreux 6:13, 16; before ἐν (εἰς), as in Heb. (El., § 39, 4), Matthieu 5:34, 36 23:16, 18 23:20-22 Apocalypse 10:6 (Bl., § 70, 3).†

G3661.def:
ὁμοθυμαδόν
(ὁμός, θυμός), [in LXX for יַחַד (frequently in Jb), Wis.10:20 18:5, 12, al. ;] 
with one mind, with one accord: Actes 1:14 2:46 4:24 5:12 7:57 8:6 12:20 15:25 18:12 19:29, Romains 15:6 (Hatch, Essays, 63 f., argues that the un-cl. sense together, which is found in Job 3:18 38:33, Nombres 24:24, Wis.18:5, 12 (but not Wis.10:20), al., should be attached to the NT instances, but see Abbott, Essays, 96; MM, xviii).†

G3662.def:
ὁμοιάζω
(ὅμοιος), 
to be like: Matthieu 23:27 (L, Tr., txt., WH, mg.) Matthieu 26:73 (WH, mg.) (not found elsewhere. cf. παρ-ομοιάζω.) †

G3663.def:
ὁμοιοπαθής, -ές
(ὅμοιος, πάσχω), [in LXX: Wis.7:3, 4Ma.12:13 * ;] 
of like feelings or affections: with dative, Actes 14:15, Jacques 5:17.†

G3664.def:
ὅμοιος, -οία, -οιον 
[in LXX for כְּמוֹ, etc. ;] 
like, resembling, such as, the same as: with dative, of form or appearance, Jean 9:9, Apocalypse 1:13 (WH, mg., R, but see infr.) Apocalypse 1:15 2:18 4:6-7 9:7, 10 (B1., § 37, 62) Rev_9:19; Rev_11:1; Rev_13:2; Rev_13:11; ὁράσει, Rev_4:3; of nature, condition, ability, etc., Mat_22:39, Act_17:29, Gal_5:21, 1Jn_3:2, Rev_13:4; Rev_18:18; Rev_21:11; Rev_21:18; of comparison in parables, Mat_13:31 ff. Mat_20:1, Luk_13:18-19; Luk_13:21; of thinking, acting, etc., Mat_11:16; Mat_13:52, Luk_6:47-49; Luk_7:31-32 (T, with genitive; 131., § 36, 11) Luk_12:36, Joh_8:55, Jud_1:7; with accusative, Rev_1:13 (WH, txt.; Swete, Hort, in l) Rev_14:14.†

G3665.def:
ὁμοιότης, -ητος, ἡ
(ὅμοιος), [in LXX: Genèse 1:11-12 (מִין), Wis.14:19, 4Ma.15:4 * ;] 
likeness: καθ᾽ ὁμοιότητα, in like manner, Hébreux 4:15; id. with genitive (MM, xviii), after the likeness (of), Hébreux 7:15.†

G3666.def:
ὁμοιόω, -ῶ
(ὅμοιος), [in LXX chiefly for דָּמָה ;] 
__1. to make like, with genitive and dative; pass., to be made or become like: Matthieu 6:8 13:24 18:23 22:2 25:1, Actes 14:11, Hébreux 2:17; before ὡς (cf. Eze.32:2, Heb.), Romains 9:29. 
__2. to liken, compare: with dative, accusative, Matthieu 11:16, Luc 7:31 13:18, 20; πῶς όμοιώσωμεν, Marc 4:30; pass., Matthieu 7:24, 26 (cf. ἀφ-ομοιόω).†

G3668.def:
ὁμοίως
(ὅμοιος), 
adv., 
likewise, in like manner, equally: Matthieu 22:26, Marc 4:16, Luc 10:37, al.; with dative, Matthieu 22:39, Luc 6:31; ὁ. καί, Matthieu 22:26, Marc 15:31, al.; ὁ. καθώς, Luc 17:28; καθὼς . . . ὁ., Luc 6:31; ὁ. μέντοι καί, Ju 8

G3669.def:
ὁμοίωσις, -εως, ἡ
(ὁμοιόω) [in LXX chiefly for דְּמוּת, Psaumes 58:4, al. ;] 
__1. a making like, becoming like (Plat.). 
__2. likeness: Jacques 3:9 (LXX).† 
SYN.: see: ὁμοίωμα, and cf. Tr., Syn., § xv

G3670.def:
ὁμολογέω, -ῶ
(ὁμόλογος, of one mind: Dan LXX Su 1:60 *), [in LXX: Job 40:9 (14) (יָדָה hi.), Jérémie 44:25 (נָדַר), al. ;] 
__1. to speak the same language (Hdt.). 
__2. to agree with (Hdt., Plat., al.). 
__3. to agree, confess, acknowledge (Plat., al.) : absol., Jean 1:20 12:42; pass., Romains 10:10; before ὅτι, ib., Hébreux 11:13; with accusative of thing(s), Actes 23:8, 1 Jean 1:9, Apocalypse 3:5; id. with dative of person(s), Actes 24:14; with accusative cogn., 1 Timothée 6:12; with accusative of person(s), 1 Jean 2:23 Jn 4:3; id. before pred. accusative (Bl., § 34, 5; 73, 5), Jean 9:22, Romains 10:9, 1 Jean 4:2 Jn 4:15, 2Jn.7; with inf. (M, Pr., 229), Tite 1:16; with dative of person(s) before ὅτι, Matthieu 7:23; before ἐν, with dative of person(s) (M, Pr., 104; Bl., § 41, 2), Matthieu 10:32, Luc 12:8. 
__4. to agree, promise: τ. ἐπαγγελίαν, Actes 7:17; with inf. obj. (Bl., § 61, 3), Matthieu 14:7. 
__5. = ἐξμολογέω, to praise: Hébreux 13:15 (Westc., in l). 
(cf. ἀνθ-ομολογέομοι, ἐξμολογέω.) †

G3671.def:
ὁμολογία, -ας, ἡ
(όμολογέω), [in LXX: Deutéronome 12:6, 17. Amos 4:5, Eze.46:12 (נְדָבָה), Lévitique 22:18, Jérémie 44:25 (נֶדֶר), I Esther 9:8 * ;] 
__1. in cl., an agreement assent, compact (in π., of a contract; Deiss., BS, 249). 
__2. confession (prob. always in an objective sense): 2 Corinthiens 9:13, 1 Timothée 6:12-13 Hébreux 3:1 4:14 10:13.†

G3672.def:
ὁμολογουμένως 
adv. (ὁμ oλογέω), [in LXX: 4Ma.6:31 4Mac 7:16 4Mac 16:1 * ;] 
__1. as agreed, conformably with. 
__2. confessedly, by common consent: 1 Timothée 3:16.†

G3673.def:
ὁμότεχνος, -ον
(ὁμός, τέχνη), 
practising the same craft, of the same trade: Actes 18:3.†

G3675.def:
ὁμόφρων, -ον
(ὁμός, φρήν), = ὁμόνοος, 
agreeing, of one mind: 1 Pierre 3:8.†

G3676.def:
ὅμως 
adv. (ὁμίς), 
yet: ὅ. μέντοι, 
but yet, nevertheless, Jean 12:42; by hyperbaton, out of its proper position, 1 Corinthiens 14:7, Galates 3:15 (but see Bl., § 77, 14).†

G3677.def:
ὄναρ, τό 
indecl., used only in nom, and accusative sing. (the other cases are supplied by ὄνειρος), a dream: κατ᾽ ὄ. (in later writers only), in a dream, Matthieu 1:20 2:12-13, 19 2:22 27:19.†

G3678.def:
ὀνάριον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of ὄνος), 
a young ass: Jean 12:14.†

G3679.def:
ὀνειδίζω
(ὄνειδος), [in LXX chiefly for חָרַף pi. ;] 
to reproach, upbraid: absol., Jacques 1:5; with accusative of person(s) (in cl. more frequently with dative of person(s); Bl., § 34, 2; WM, 278), Matthieu 5:11, Marc 15:32, 34, WH, mg., Luc 6:22, Romains 15:3" (LXX) ; τ. πόλεις, Matthieu 11:20; pass., 1 Timothée 4:10, WH, mg., 1 Pierre 4:14; with accusative of thing(s), Marc 16:14; with dupl. accusative, Matthieu 27:44.†

G3680.def:
ὀνειδισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ὀνειδίζω) [in LXX chiefly for חֶרְפָּה ;] 
a reproach: Romains 15:3, Hébreux 10:33; εἰς ὀ. ἐμπεαεῖν, 1 Timothée 3:7; ὁ ὀ. τοῦ Χριστοῦ Hébreux 11:26 13:13.†

G3681.def:
ὄνειδος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for חֶרְפָּה, also for כְּלִמָּה, etc. ;] 
__1. reproach, censure, blame. 
__2. matter of reproach, disgrace: Luc 1:25.†

G3682.def:
Ὀνήσιμος, -ου, ὁ
(i.e. profitable, ὄνησις, profit), 
Onesimus: Colossiens 4:9, Phm 10 (a common name among slaves; see MM, iii, xviii).†

G3683.def:
Ὀνησίφορος, -ου, ὁ
(i.e. bringing advantage), 
Onesiphorus: 2 Timothée 1:16 4:19.†

G3684.def:
ὀνικός, -ή, -όν
(ὄνος), 
of or for an ass. μύλος ὀ., Matthieu 18:6, Marc 9:42 (elsewhere only in π.; see MM, xviii).†

G3685.def:
ὀνίνημι 
[in LXX: Tob.3:8, Sir.30:2 * ;] 
to profit, benefit, help; mid., to have profit, derive benefit: optative (M, Pr., 195), with genitive, Phm 20.†

G3686.def:
ὄνομα, -τος, τό, 
[in LXX chiefly for שֵׁם ;] 
__1. in general, the name by which a person or thing is called: Matthieu 10:2, Marc 3:16, Luc 1:63, Jean 18:10, al.; ἄνθρωπος (etc.), ᾧ (οὗ) ὄ. (τ. ὄ), sc. ἦν or ἐστίν (BL, §30, 3), Marc 14:32, Luc 1:26, 27; with same ellipsis, καὶ τ. ὄ. αὐτοῦ, Luc 1:5, Jean 1:6, al.; ὀνόματι, before nom. prop., Matthieu 27:32, Marc 5:22, Luc 1:5, Actes 5:1, al.; accusative absol. (Bl., §34, 7), τοὔνομα (= τ. ὄνομα), Matthieu 27:57; ὄ. μοι (sc. ἐστίν; cf. Hom., Od., ix, 366), Marc 5:9 (cf. Luc 8:30); ἔξειν ὄ., Apocalypse 9:11; καλεῖν (ἐπιτιθέναι) ὄ. (Bl., §33, 1), Matthieu 1:21, Marc 3:16; τ. ὄ. ἐν (τ.) βίβλῳ ζωῆς (cf. Deiss., LAE, 121), Philippiens 4:3, Apocalypse 13:8, cf. Luc 10:20 (ἐν τ. οὐρανοῖς); ὄ. βλασφημίας, Apocalypse 13:1; the name as opposite to the reality, Apocalypse 3:1 (cf. Hdt., vii, 138); as a title: Éphésiens 1:21, Philippiens 2:9, 10 (Lft., in l.). 
__2. By a usage similar to that with ref. to Heb. שֵׁם (Lft., Notes, 106f.), but also common in Hellenistic (M, Pr., 100; Bl., §39, 4; Deiss, BS, 146f., 196f.; LAE, 123:4, of all that the name implies, of rank, authority, character, etc.: of acting on one's authority or in his behalf, ἐν (εἰς) ὄ., with genitive of person(s) (see reff. supr.), Matthieu 10:41 21:9 28:19, Marc 11:9, Luc 13:35, Jean 5:43, Actes 8:16, 1 Corinthiens 1:13; of the name Christian, 1 Pierre 4:16; esp. of the name of God as expressing the divine attributes: ἁγιάζειν (ἅγιον) τὸ ὄ. (τ. Πατρός, Κυρίου), Matthieu 6:9, Luc 1:49 11:2; ψάλλειν (ὁμολογεῖν) τῷ ὀ., Romains 15:9, Hébreux 13:15; δοξάζειν (φανεροῦν, φοβεῖσθαι) τὸ ὄ., Jean 12:28 17:6, 26 Apocalypse 11:18 15:4; βλασφημεῖν, Romains 2:24, 1 Timothée 6:1, Apocalypse 13:6; similarly, of the name of Christ: τ. καλὂν ὄ. (Deiss., LAE, 276); πιστεύειν τῷ ὀ., 1 Jean 3:23; π. εἰς τ. ὄ. (Bl., §39, 4), Jean 1:12 2:23 3:18; ὀνομάζειν τὸ ὄ., 2 Timothée 2:19; κρατεῖν, Apocalypse 2:13; οὐκ ἀρνεῖσθαι, Apocalypse 3:8; ἐν τ. ὀ. (see reff. supr.), Marc 9:38 16:[17], Luc 10:17, Jean 14:13 16:23, 24 20:31, Actes 3:6 4:12, Éphésiens 5:20, 1 Pierre 4:14, al.; εἰς τ. ὄ. συνάγεσθαι, Matthieu 18:20; ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀ., Matthieu 19:29; διὰ τὸ ὄ., Matthieu 10:22, Marc 13:13, al.; διὰ τοῦ ὀ., 1 Corinthiens 1:10; ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀ., Actes 9:16, Romains 1:5, al.; id. absol., Actes 5:41, 3Jo.7; πρὸς τὸ ὄ., Actes 26:9. 
__3. cause, ground, reason (in cl., usually in bad sense, pretext): Marc 9:41 (Swete, in l.; Dalman, Words, 305f.). 
__4. In late Greek (Deiss., BS., 196f.), an individual, a person: Actes 1:15, Apocalypse 3:4 11:13.

G3687.def:
ὀνομάζω
(ὄνομα), [in LXX for זָכַר, נָקַב, קָרָא ;] 
__1. to name, mention, or address by name: Actes 19:13; pass., Romains 15:20, Éphésiens 1:21 5:3; of the use of the Divine name in praise and worship, 2 Timothée 2:19 (LXX, Nombres 16:26; cf. Ésaïe 52:11, Amos 6:10). 
__2. to name, call, give a name to: Marc 3:14 (T, R, txt. om.), Luc 6:13-14; pass., 1 Corinthiens 5:11; before ἐξ (cl.), Éphésiens 3:15 (cf. ἐπ-ονομάζω).†

G3688.def:
ὄνος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for חֲמוֹר, also for אָתוֹן, etc. ;] 
an ass: Matthieu 21:2, 5" (LXX), Luc 14:5, Jean 12:15" (LXX) ; ὁ, Luc 13:15; ἡ, Matthieu 21:7 .†

G3689.def:
ὄντως 
adv. (ὤν, ptcp. of εἰμί, sum) [in LXX: Nombres 22:37 (אׇמְנָם), Jérémie 3:23 (אָכֵן), Jérémie 10:19 (אַךְ), 3Ki.12:24, Wis.17:14 * ;] 
really, actually, truly: Marc 11:32, Luc 23:47 24:34, Jean 8:36, 1 Corinthiens 14:25, Galates 3:21 4:1-31 ἡ ὄ. ζωή, 1 Timothée 6:19; ἡ ὄ. χήρα, 1 Timothée 5:3 5:5 5:16 †

G3690.def:
ὄξος, -εος (-ους), τό
(ὄξύς), [in LXX: Nombres 6:3, Ruth 2:14, Psaumes 69:21, Proverbes 25:20 (חֹמֶץ)* ;] 
sour wine (posca, vin-Deu pays), the ordinary drink of labourers and common soldiers: Matthieu 27:48, Marc 15:36, Luc 23:36, Jean 19:29-30.†

G3691.def:
ὄξύς, -εῖα, -ύ 
[in LXX: Psaumes 57:4, al. (חַד), Amos 2:15 (קַל), Ésaïe 5:28 (שָׁנַן), etc. ;] 
__1. sharp: Apocalypse 1:16 2:12 14:14, 17-18 19:15. 
__2. Of motion, swift: Romains 3:15 (LXX ταχινός).†

G3692.def:
ὀπή, -ῆς, ἡ 
[in LXX for חוֹר, חֲגָו, etc. ;] 
an opening, a hole: Jacques 3:11 (cf. Exode 33:22), Hébreux 11:33 (cf. Ob 3).†

G3693.def:
ὄπισθεν 
adv. of place, [in LXX chiefly for אָחוֹר, אַחַר ;] 
behind, after: Matthieu 9:20, Marc 5:27, Luc 8:44, Apocalypse 4:6 5:1. As prep. with genitive: Matthieu 15:23, Luc 23:26, Apocalypse 1:10 (WH, mg.).†

G3695.def:
ὁπλίζω
(ὅπλον), [in Sm.: Jérémie 52:25 * ;] 
to make ready, equip; of soldiers, to arm. Mid., to arm oneself; figuratively, ἔννοιαν: 1 Pierre 4:1 (cf. θράσος ὁ., Soph., Elec., 995), (cf. καθ-ὁπλίζω).†

G3696.def:
ὅπλον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX for מָגֵן, צִנָּה, etc. ;] 
__1. a tool, implement, instrument: ὅπλα ἀδικίας (Opp. to ὅ. δικαιοσύνης), Romains 6:13. 
__2. Freq., in pl., arms, weapons: Jean 18:3, 2 Corinthiens 10:4; metaphorically, τ. φωτός, Romains 13:12; τ. δικαιοσύνης, 2 Corinthiens 6:7.†

G3697.def:
ὁποῖος, -οία, -οῖον 
[in LXX: Cantique des cantiques 5:10, 2Ma.11:37 * ;] 
of what sort: 1 Corinthiens 3:13, Galates 2:6, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:9, Jacques 1:24; τοιοῦτος ὁ., such as, Actes 26:29.†

G3699.def:
ὅπου 
adv. 
of place, correlat. of ποῦ (which see), where. 
__I. Prop., of place, 
__1. where; 
__(a) in relative sentences, with indic: Matthieu 25:24, 26, Marc 2:4 4:5, 15 5:40 13:14, Jean 3:8 6:62 7:34, 36 11:32 14:3 17:24 20:19, Romains 15:20, Apocalypse 2:13; after nouns of place, for relat. prepositional phrase (ἐν ᾧ., etc.), Matthieu 6:19-20 13:5 26:57 28:6, Marc 6:55 9:48 Luc 12:33, Jean 1:28 4:20, 46 6:23 7:42 10:40 11:30 12:1 18:1, 20 19:18, 20 19:41 20:12, Actes 17:1, Apocalypse 2:13 11:8 20:10; before ἐκεῖ., Matthieu 6:21, Luc 12:34 17:37 Jean 12:26; id. pleonast. (= Heb. שָׁם . . . אֲשֶׁר; Aram. תַּמָּן . . דּ; of. Genèse 13:3), ὅ. . . . ἐκεῖ, Apocalypse 12:6, 14; ὅ. . . . ἐπ᾽ αὐτῶν, Apocalypse 17:9; ὅ. ἄν, wherever (M, Pr., 168), with imperfect indic., Marc 6:56; with Pres. subjc., Matthieu 24:28; ὅ. ἐάν, Matthieu 26:13, Marc 6:10 9:18 14:9, 14 a; 
__(b) in quaest. indir., with aor. subjc.: Marc 14:14 b, Luc 22:11. 
__2. In late writers (sometimes also in cl.; Bl., § 25, 2), with verbs of motion, = ὅποι, whither: with indic., Jean 8:21-22 13:33, 36 14:4 21:18, Hébreux 6:20, Jacques 3:4; ὅ. ἄν, whithersoever, with present ind., Apocalypse 14:4; subjc., Luc 9:57; ὅ. ἐάν, Matthieu 8:19. 
__II. Without strict local sense, 
__1. of time or condition: Colossiens 3:11, Hébreux 9:16 10:18, Jacques 3:16, 2 Pierre 2:11. 
__2. Of cause or reason (AV, whereas): 1 Corinthiens 3:3.†
